title: Contain and restore focus in the palette and feed drawer
body:
## Summary
The search palette and the narrow activity drawer declare aria-modal but do not trap Tab or restore focus.

## Description
GlobalSearchPanel/index.tsx:53 and ActivityFeedPanel/index.tsx:181 set aria-modal="true" with no Tab handling and no focus restore; the feed drawer also never moves focus inside. The shared ui/Modal already implements trap, initial focus and restore (ui/Modal.tsx:18-21). Fixed means both surfaces use that behaviour, extracted if the Modal shell cannot host their layout.

## Flow
- open the palette, press Tab past the last control -> focus leaves into the inert-looking page
- close it -> focus falls to body instead of the trigger
- build: extract the trap from ui/Modal as a hook, apply to both surfaces

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users stay inside the modal and return to where they were. Could break: the palette input must keep focus for typing and arrow keys.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - modal surfaces hold and restore focus
Before: 2 aria-modal surfaces, 0 with a trap or restore (read of both files; no focus-trap hook in src)
After: predicted 2 of 2
Method: simulation - walked Tab and close on both; extraction touches ui/Modal, outside this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: component test: Tab from last control stays in dialog; closing returns focus to the opener

title: Expose the palette active row to assistive tech
body:
## Summary
Arrow keys move a purely visual highlight in the palette; a screen reader hears nothing.

## Description
useGlobalSearchPanel.ts handleKeyDown moves activeIndex, painted only by a background class in SearchResultRow.tsx:43. The input has no combobox role, aria-controls or aria-activedescendant, and the list has no listbox role. Rows hold a nested Run button, so a plain listbox of options is invalid; the choice is combobox+grid or a live announcement of the active row.

## Flow
- focus the palette, type, press ArrowDown -> no announcement of the selected row
- build: choose grid vs live-region, then wire ids and roles

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users can use the palette arrow model. Could break: existing tests find the input by role textbox.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - active row is exposed
Before: 0 of 3 ARIA links present (role, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant)
After: predicted 3 of 3
Method: simulation - attribute read; the pattern choice is the open question
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: test: after ArrowDown the input aria-activedescendant names the active row and that id exists

title: Stop FTS highlight markers colliding with literal arrows
body:
## Summary
Search highlighting uses the printable arrows as markers, so a title containing an arrow renders a stray highlight and loses the character in recents.

## Description
search-index.ts:226-227 asks FTS5 for snippet markers with the arrow characters; helpers.ts:9-10 turns every arrow into a mark tag, and recentSelections.ts:40 and SearchResultRow.tsx:37 strip them. module-registry.ts has 10 lines with arrows, so indexed text can contain them. Fixed means private-use marker characters server and client, or matcher offsets.

## Flow
- search a term in a title with a literal arrow -> an unbalanced mark highlights the rest
- select it -> the recent title loses the arrow
- build: swap the marker pair in search-index and the 3 client readers together

## Expected impact
Highlights and recent titles match the source text. Could break: persisted recents keep their already-stripped titles.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - highlight marks only real hits
Before: 3 client sites treat every arrow as a marker; 10 registry lines contain one
After: predicted 0 collisions
Method: simulation - search-index.ts is outside this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: unit test: highlightMarkers on a title with a literal arrow yields no mark tag

title: Move the project dropdown Escape onto the hotkey registry
body:
## Summary
The project dropdown runs its own document keydown listener for Escape instead of the LIFO layer stack.

## Description
useTopBar.ts:53-95 handles Escape on document, while the palette and feed use useEscapeLayer (useGlobalSearchPanel.ts:59, ActivityFeedPanel/index.tsx:50). One Escape can therefore close the dropdown and a registered layer together. Fixed means useEscapeLayer owns Escape and the document listener keeps only the Tab trap, with focus return preserved.

## Flow
- open the dropdown and another layer, press Escape -> both react
- build: useEscapeLayer in useTopBar, close callback returns focus to the trigger

## Expected impact
Escape closes one layer at a time everywhere in the shell. Could break: the rename field Escape relies on stopPropagation added tonight (3f449e77).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one Escape owner
Before: 1 raw Escape listener beside 2 registry layers in this context
After: predicted 0 raw listeners
Method: simulation - no test yet stacks the dropdown with a layer
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: test: dropdown open with a pushed layer; one Escape closes only the topmost
